question.prompt:
After school, Maya and Naomi headed to the beach, \(6\) miles away. Maya decided to bike while Naomi took a bus. The graph below shows their journeys, indicating the time and distance traveled. What was the difference, in miles per hour, between Naomi’s and Maya’s average speeds?

[Figure 1](figures/2020_AMC_8_Q11_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
For average speed, use the full journey time, including any stops. The graph shows that Maya covers \(6\) miles in \(30\) minutes, while Naomi covers the same distance in \(10\) minutes.

Convert those times to hours:

\[
v_{\text{Maya}}=\frac6{1/2}=12,\qquad
v_{\text{Naomi}}=\frac6{1/6}=36.
\]

Their average speeds differ by \(36-12=\boxed{24}\) miles per hour, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\). The bends and flat parts of the graphs matter through the total elapsed time.
solutions.title: Read total journey times and compute average speeds
